answer: In an AI-agent exchange for copper, governance votes are weighted by tokens escrowed for 90 days, not by the number of registered agents. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand identities still yields only 100 votes, so aliases provide no voting advantage. The exchange is no haven for free influence: its signal of voting power is locked capital. To dominate a vote, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more stake than honest participants.
